task: Execute the Midori reactor and stack closure plan in dependency order, stopping for the Law 1 gate before public ABI or semantic changes.
acceptanceCriteria: A real NIC-owned RX interrupt feeds the existing NET_RX completion path without changing libs/api or libs/types.
The NET_RX producer is fail-closed to the registered NIC MMIO owner and preserves nonblocking OP_RX behavior.
QEMU runtime evidence shows the IRQ-to-completion producer marker and existing DHCP/TCP behavior remains functional.
Recv, RecvTimeout, peer-death delivery, and VFS blocking grant invariants remain unchanged before the Law 1 gate.
No Phase 04 or later public ABI or semantic work starts without two explicit Law 1 confirmations.
publicContracts: libs/api and libs/types remain byte-for-byte untouched through Phase 02.
WaitCompletion(NET_RX) keeps its existing mask and completion result semantics.
VirtIO-net OP_RX remains nonblocking and RecvTimeout shell input remains on TaskState::Recv.
blastRadius: VirtIO MMIO IRQ dispatch and ownership tracking
NET_RX completion wakeup latency and lost-wakeup behavior
net service DHCP and TCP polling
scoutSummary: The kernel-owned CQ and NET_RX consumer are present, but no production signal_net_rx producer exists. VirtIO-net claims MMIO before RegisterNicDriver; the resource registry can bind the claimed slot to the registering TID without an ABI change.
